correctness.rationale: Re-audited /workspace/repairs/3/. In the frozen text, strictness for a merely nonconstant nondecreasing observable can fail: if μ is uniform on [1,2], 1_{x>1} is pointwise nonconstant even on [1,2] but is almost surely constant for both marks. The repair explicitly requires nonconstancy μ-a.s. and proves it by the two-independent-draw covariance identity with the strictly increasing likelihood ratio; the terminal mixture scales the strict expectation gap by 1−e^(−κm). The reported total of 26 independent assertions was not justified by the checker (e.g. the Beta test returns six but has two assert statements sharing error estimates); the affected verification prose and diagnostic reporting were corrected without altering the tests or frozen verification front matter. Independently reconstructed the core claim: solving Df''=rf with the two exit boundary conditions gives the upper and lower killed-hit weights; summing repeated reset-only excursions gives the normalized sinh tilt for the first threshold-origin. The final excursion of a fresh process has normalized e^(−κx) weights by geometric renewal. Conditional on first reaching m, strong Markov and clock memorylessness give e^(−κm) probability of absorption in that same excursion, otherwise the fresh terminal mark is independent. This proves the exact joint measure and covariance. For nonatomic μ the product has zero diagonal mass, attaining the TV bound. Compact-support exponential comparisons give the unscaled endpoints; the stated density asymptotics give the scaled Gamma laws by endpoint substitution and dominated convergence, and uniform e^(−κm)≤e^(−κb) removes the same-excursion component for every allowed threshold sequence. An independent two-atom calculation gives the stated tilt weights and covariance 0.007273218022307203. The frozen diagnostic code was inspected, not executed; the conditional law and asymptotics are analytical.
